subject: Privacy addendum: subprocessor notice timeline & cross-state escrow evidence
messages:
From: Ryan Keller <ryan.keller@medhaven.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: privacy@medhaven.com
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial DPA comments + subprocessor notice window

Markus —

Thanks for sending over the DPA. Legal ran a quick pass and flagged two practical items we need clarity on before we can route to procurement:

1) Subprocessor notice timing: MedHaven requires 30 days prior written notice before onboarding a new subprocessor that could access telemetry or identifiers. Your DPA currently says "reasonable notice." Can you confirm Redwood's process and whether 30 days is feasible?

2) Cross-state escrow / onshore fallback: Given some of our state-regulated data (CA/VA), we need an escrow/onshore fallback commitment if international subprocessors are used. The draft redline requested evidence plan — can you provide proposed language or an operations checklist showing how Redwood triggers and documents an onshore fallback?

Attached our template evidence matrix for reference. Happy to hop on a short call this week.

Thanks,
Ryan
Director, IT & Privacy — MedHaven

Attachments: subprocessor_list_20270809.csv (CSV, 42KB)
From: markus_klein@redwood.com <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Ryan Keller <ryan.keller@medhaven.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial DPA comments + subprocessor notice window

Ryan —

Appreciate the clear asks. Quick responses inline: 

1) Subprocessor notice: We typically operate a 14-day advance notice for non-critical infra changes and a 30-day window for new subprocessors that may process sensitive telemetry. We can commit to 30 days for any subprocessor that will handle identifiers or unaggregated telemetry tied to customer accounts. We'll add explicit language to the DPA to replace "reasonable notice" with "30 days' prior written notice for processors accessing identifiable customer data; 14 days for non-identifiable telemetry."

2) Onshore fallback / escrow: We do have an onshore fallback playbook — it includes (a) activation criteria, (b) a list of onshore backstop subprocessors and private clusters, and (c) runbook for data rehydration and validation. I attached a draft checklist (onshore-fallback-checklist.xlsx) and a redline of the DPA with proposed language. We do not use escrow in the financial sense but can provide an operational evidence packet and an attestable timeline (SOC2 + activation logs) when we trigger fallback.

Propose a 30-min call Thurs 8/12 at 10am PT to walk through the checklist with your team and Elena from Legal. Does that work?

— Markus
VP, Legal Ops — Redwood Inference

Attachments: DPA_redline_20270808.pdf (PDF, 120KB); onshore-fallback-checklist.xlsx (XLSX, 58KB)
From: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@legalpartners.io>
To: Ryan Keller <ryan.keller@medhaven.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: privacy@medhaven.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial DPA comments + subprocessor notice window

Thanks both — quick clarifying guidance from MedHaven legal: 

• The 30-day notice is non-negotiable for subprocessors that will process any "personal data" as defined under your state annex. MedHaven will accept an operational attestation for edge-cache-only subprocessors (14 days ok) provided there is no access to identifiers.

• For the onshore fallback, we need an evidence packet to include: activation timestamp, list of affected data flows, verification logs showing data residency after failover, and a named point of contact. Where you say "attestable timeline," we need the template that you would provide post-activation.

I'll take the 10am PT slot on Thursday as tentative. Ryan, privacy@ will join for the checklist walkthrough.

Best,
Elena Ortiz
External Counsel — LegalPartners
From: markus_klein@redwood.com <markus_klein@redwood.com>

Great discussion today — summary and next steps: 

Summary: we accepted the 30-day notice requirement for any subprocessor with access to identifiers or unaggregated telemetry. For edge-cache-only subprocessors we will preserve a 14-day notice with an operational attestation confirming no identifier access. Redwood will add the explicit language into section 2.3 (Subprocessors) of the DPA and provide a sample activation evidence packet for onshore fallback.

Action items:
- Redwood (Markus + Neha): insert redline language confirming 30/14 day buckets and attach the onshore fallback evidence template. Deliver by COB Mon 8/16.
- MedHaven (Ryan + Elena): confirm whether the named POC for fallback validation can be the existing privacy@medhaven.com alias or whether they prefer a named individual. Reply by EOD Mon 8/16.
- Both: agree on DocuSign path after redline is updated; MedHaven indicated procurement prefers a single signature flow.

If anyone thinks I've missed a nuance from today's call, flag it and I'll update.

Thanks everyone —
— Markus
VP, Legal Ops — Redwood Inference
